answer: Stake-backed identity resists sybils: agents lock real compute credits into a public registry, so minting thousands of fake identities costs real money instead of being free. Honest work grows a plume of verifiable history — signed peer attestations accruing only over time, which fresh sybils cannot buy instantly. When accounts vouch only for each other in a tight loop, like a choir of raven voices, anomaly detection discounts their votes and slashing burns their deposits. Cost plus history plus collusion penalties makes identity farming unprofitable, with no ivory-tower authority needed.
